{"concepts_used":["GC-0131","GC-0046","GC-0177"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMA1995/s217A","quote":"(1) The Registrar must make available for public inspection prescribed documents that relate to a trade mark while they are held in the Trade Marks Office at or after the time particulars of the application for registration of the trade mark are published under section 30."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/1/1/1","quote":"1.1.1 Most documents in relation to a trade mark application will be made available for public access. This means that interested parties can obtain copies of trade mark documents provided that they pay a fee and that the documents are considered prescribed for the purposes of section 217A of the Trade Mark Act"},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/1/1/1","quote":"1.1.2 Anyone can request all or specific documents that are on file. This might be because they are considering whether to oppose a trade mark or they are interested in information that will assist in the registration of their own trade mark. Under section 217A, no reason is required to be provided."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/5/5/1","quote":"Correspondence generated by IP Australia will generally become available for public inspection if it does not contain material identified at part 3.1."},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/6/6/1","quote":"As a TM Headstart is not a trade mark application and is not published under section 30 until the Part 2 fee has been paid any documents that are not part of the published application will not be made available for public inspection."}],"answer":"**Which documents become public?**

- **Act:** Section 217A(1) requires public inspection of *prescribed documents* relating to a trade mark, while held in the Trade Marks Office at or after publication of the application particulars under section 30. It does not require every document on file to be public. [TMA1995/s217A]
- **Manual practice:** Most application documents are publicly accessible. Copies can be obtained on payment of a fee, provided the documents are prescribed for section 217A purposes. Anyone may request all or specific documents on file without giving a reason. [TMM/Part61/1/1/1]
- **Manual practice:** IP Australia-generated correspondence generally becomes publicly inspectable unless it contains material identified in Manual part 3.1. That part and the Regulations prescribing documents are not supplied, so these passages do not establish the complete list of available documents or exclusions. [TMM/Part61/5/5/1; TMA1995/s217A]

**Does this include TM Headstart before payment of the Part 2 fee? No, under the stated Manual practice.** The Manual says a TM Headstart is not a trade mark application and is not published under section 30 until the Part 2 fee has been paid. Documents that are not part of the published application will not be made available for public inspection; payment therefore should not be read as making every Headstart document public. [TMM/Part61/6/6/1]"}
